papers.title: EchoWM: Open and Enterable Omnimodal World Models

summary.tldr: EchoWM is an omnimodal world model that enables continuous camera navigation while simultaneously generating 720p video, environmental sound, speech, and music across first-person and third-person perspectives.
key_points: Maps discrete commands and continuous poses to a shared metric-scale relative 6-DoF trajectory calibrated across datasets.
Learns camera-character dynamics for third-person scenes directly from data without requiring view-specific controllers.
Uses a progressive training strategy followed by autoregressive post-training to enable long-horizon, audio-visually synchronized generation.
summary.why_it_matters: It unifies multi-modal generation with flexible 6-DoF trajectory control, enabling interactive, synchronized audio-visual media generation for virtual environments.

papers.title: Annotations as Rollouts: Efficient and Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Video MLLMs

summary.tldr: OraRL integrates ground-truth annotations as oracle rollouts during video MLLM post-training, using a decoupled advantage estimator and sign-balanced pruning to bypass slow chain-of-thought generation while improving performance.
key_points: Directly integrating high-reward oracle rollouts causes 'advantage inversion' by raising group baselines and making positive policy advantages negative.
OraRL uses a decoupled advantage estimator where policy rollouts define an oracle-free baseline, modulated by the oracle-policy gap via directional gain and a detached oracle advantage.
Sign-balanced pruning retains only the oracle and strongest positive/negative rollouts, dropping step-time overhead to 2.2x SFT compared to 4.9x for GRPO with CoT.
Without CoT, Video-ORA-9B reduces decoding latency from 4,780 ms to 130 ms while scaling effectively from 0.8B to 9B parameters across 100k prompts.
Video-ORA-9B achieves state-of-the-art results: temporal mIoU of 66.0 (up from 62.5), tracking AO of 78.2 (up from 73.0), segmentation of 70.4 (up from 64.3), and 73.1 on VSI-Bench.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables highly efficient RL post-training for video MLLMs, dramatically cutting decoding latency while outperforming substantially larger commercial models like GPT-5 and Gemini-3-Pro on spatial and temporal intelligence benchmarks.

papers.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report

summary.tldr: Tencent introduced WeMM-Embedding, a family of universal multimodal embedding models (2B, 4B, and 9B) supporting text, images, videos, visual documents, and interleaved multimodal inputs with flexible output dimensions.
key_points: Training uses a two-stage approach: large-scale multimodal alignment followed by refinement via curated data, fine-grained relevance supervision, and cross-scale knowledge transfer.
The 2B model outperforms prior 8B open-source baselines on MMEB-v2, while the 9B model sets a new state-of-the-art score of 80.6.
Model performance was validated across a 26-task internal benchmark and 14 online A/B tests, leading to deployment in production systems like WeChat Channels, Search, and Moments.
summary.why_it_matters: WeMM-Embedding provides open-source, high-efficiency multimodal embedding models that outperform larger baselines and have proven scalable efficacy in production recommendation and search environments.

papers.title: AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces

summary.tldr: AutoSaddler is an automatic agent harness optimization framework that treats harnesses as code and uses offline mini-batch execution traces to iteratively diagnose failures, generate patches, and select updates.
key_points: Formulates agent harness improvement as an offline learning task using failure-trace diagnosis, structured patch generation, and validation-based selection.
Improves task performance across benchmark suites, adding 9.0 percentage points on GAIA2, 9.6 points on SWE-Bench Pro, and 10.0 points on Terminal-Bench 2.0 over base harnesses.

Relies on three critical components: deep debugging over shallow reflection, targeted harness code edits over unconstrained prompt editing, and generalization-aware validation over single-trajectory repairs.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating harness design removes the manual effort required to optimize complex agent prompts, tools, and control flow for long-horizon execution tasks.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: DiffusionOPSD converts image-level reward guidance into bounded positive and negative targets for intermediate denoising predictions using an on-policy self-distillation framework with frozen behavior policies and finite fitting.
key_points: Converts endpoint rewards into explicit clean-output target predictions at sampled queries generated by a frozen behavior policy.
Uses reward gradients to construct bounded targets around anchors, which the trainable policy fits as detached supervision before updating the behavior policy via exponential moving average.
Decouples target construction from finite realization, showing through controlled same-query experiments that target-construction gains do not directly guarantee realized gains after one update.
Achieved top held-out scores in 19 of 20 reward-matched settings, outperforming competing methods by up to 44.0%.
Reduces training GPU-hours relative to DiffusionNFT by 40% on SD 3.5-M and 63% on Z-Image-Turbo.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves diffusion model alignment accuracy while significantly lowering compute requirements and enabling separate analysis of target generation versus target learning.

papers.title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Prefix Invariance in Attention, State-Space, and Hybrid Sequence Models

summary.tldr: Researchers formalize prefix invariance and introduce a two-forward-pass gradient-free audit that localizes causal leaks across attention, state-space, and hybrid sequence architectures where attention-mask inspection fails.
key_points: Prefix invariance requires that representations at position t remain strictly independent of future inputs at positions greater than t.
The proposed lightweight audit requires only two forward passes with no training or gradient calculations to pinpoint where causality breaks.
In 192 injected-fault trials across eight checkpoints, attention-mask inspection detected 0 defects, whereas the new audit localized 192/192 leaks.
Causal leaks can occur outside attention masks via scan operations or normalization steps.
The audit identified previously unknown causal defects in open models including Zamba2 and Nemotron-H.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard attention-mask checks are insufficient for ensuring causality, making empirical auditing essential for preventing future data leakage in complex or hybrid sequence models.

papers.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses

summary.tldr: Recuris introduces a recursive Experiential-Working Memory architecture that uses a fixed Meta-Agent to perform localized, validation-gated updates to Skill Memory based on execution evidence, preventing long-history performance degradation.
key_points: Working Memory tracks task progress and guides skill selection from Experiential Memory, replacing reliance on full interaction histories.
Execution outcomes form structured evidence that localizes failure modes specifically to individual memory components.
A fixed Meta-Agent executes validation-gated updates to Skill Memory, establishing a bounded recursive memory-evolution loop.
Recuris reduces long-horizon failures by up to 80% and improves performance on the longest tasks by +32.2 points, reaching 87.9% success with Claude Opus 5 on tau-bench.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a scalable architecture for recursive self-improvement that allows agents to handle expanding interaction horizons without getting derailed by lengthy execution histories.

papers.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) replaces action-side Policy-KL with input-side Query-KL to control query distribution shift without constraining LLM response exploration.
key_points: Replaces standard Policy-KL regularization with a Query-KL (QKL) term that bounds query distribution shift from the pre-RL reference distribution.
Applies a dataset-static, reference-derived per-query weight to bias policy updates toward queries typical of the reference distribution.
Eliminates response score functions from the QKL term, allowing QKL gradients to flow strictly through query likelihood without direct gradient pressure on response distributions.
Integrates into existing GRPO, PPO, and REINFORCE pipelines without requiring additional forward passes.
Demonstrates higher accuracy and improved stability during long-horizon training and high-temperature decoding across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: ERPO resolves the stability-exploration trade-off in LLM reinforcement learning, preventing policy drift while maintaining full action-space exploration without computational overhead.

papers.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs

summary.tldr: Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) stabilizes 4-bit compressed LLM post-training by distilling directly from the original, uncompressed teacher model rather than using hard-label QAT.
key_points: Distills a 4-bit student model directly from the original uncompressed teacher, bypassing intermediate bfloat16 compressed checkpoints.
Achieves a peak performance comparable to QAT roughly 7 times faster, avoiding training collapse and hand-tuned early stopping.
Applied to a GPT-OSS 120B to 60B to MXFP4 pipeline, yielding Hypernova-60B, which matches or exceeds its bfloat16 source on 7 of 9 benchmarks.
Reduces weight memory by approximately 4x while halving the parameter count compared to the original teacher.
Identifies a large, reproducible quality gap between different distributed-training backends during deployment.
summary.why_it_matters: QAH enables rapid, stable recovery of heavily compressed and 4-bit quantized LLMs without requiring multi-week hyperparameter searches.

papers.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out

summary.tldr: AutoResearch is a two-stage autonomous system that grounds research idea generation via multi-model cross-review and grounds execution using independent evidence-based review to prevent hallucinations.
key_points: Combines continuous domain knowledge integration, transferable insight identification, multi-model generation, and cross-review in the Idea Generation stage.
Decomposes plans into experiments using coordinated agents that iteratively implement, diagnose, and independently audit results in the Idea Execution stage.
Adapts workflow dynamically by making evidence-conditioned decisions to continue, revise, or terminate specific research directions.
Outperforms existing autonomous systems on the RSICD benchmark by increasing mean Recall from 32.84 to 34.69 while reducing audit-confirmed issue events to 5 (compared to 11-27).
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that coupling grounded idea generation with rigorous automated experimental auditing significantly reduces scientific hallucinations in autonomous AI research workflows.

papers.title: From Seeing to Acting: Smart Glasses as First-Person Intelligence Platforms

summary.tldr: This survey provides a unified framework for smart glasses as first-person intelligence platforms, introducing an L0-L5 autonomy taxonomy, hardware capability axes, application scene mapping, and deployment and evaluation protocols.
key_points: Formalizes first-person data flow and systems under energy, thermal, privacy, and feedback constraints across an L0-L5 framework.
Categorizes device hardware along eight verifiable capability axes and synthesizes literature around seven interdependent foundational capabilities.
Establishes a nine-dimensional deployment framework, a claim-conditioned evaluation protocol, and an evidence ladder ranging from lab metrics to field audits.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized framework to design, compare, and reproducibly evaluate trustworthy egocentric AI systems operating across tightly constrained hardware and real-world deployment environments.

papers.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward

summary.tldr: OPDVR combines on-policy distillation and RLVR by using a ReLU gating mechanism on trajectory correctness, eliminating extra hyperparameters while improving reasoning benchmarks.
key_points: Reformulates the implicit reward of sampled-token OPD based on trajectory correctness.
Applies a ReLU gating mechanism to enforce non-negative rewards for correct trajectories and non-positive rewards for incorrect ones.
Transforms sampled-token OPD into a valid RLVR method that integrates directly with policy gradient algorithms like GRPO.
Eliminates the hyperparameter tuning and trade-offs required by weighted combinations or heuristic switching methods.
Evaluated on six reasoning benchmarks, showing consistent performance improvements over standard OPD.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to benefit from dense teacher distillation while ensuring policy gradient updates align strictly with verifiable task success without adding hyperparameter complexity.

papers.title: LongWoF-Bench: Evaluating EvoMap Genes for Verifiable Long-Workflow Tasks

summary.tldr: LongWoF-Bench evaluates EvoMap Genes, which externalize verifier-confirmed execution trajectories into reusable structures that significantly boost long-workflow task performance across diverse language models.
key_points: Introduces LongWoF-Bench, a benchmark of 778 machine-verifiable tasks spanning code generation, agent-environment synthesis, mathematical reasoning, and rule following.
Evolved EvoMap Genes derived from 252 verifier-confirmed Claude Opus trajectories outperformed standard Skill representations by 8.7 to 15.5 percentage points across seven evaluated models.
Reference-distilled Genes failed to yield similar gains, demonstrating that structural utility relies directly on verified execution provenance rather than compact representation alone.
For Claude Opus, using evolved Genes solved 39 additional tasks over Skill while reducing solve-time token consumption by 9.9%.
summary.why_it_matters: Consolidating verified execution trajectories into structured, reusable Genes allows models to improve long-workflow success rates and lower token costs without re-discovering strategies from scratch.

papers.title: Better Retrieval, Worse Robustness:How Multi-hop RAG Amplifies Upstream ASR Errors

summary.tldr: Multi-hop RAG extensions like entity-graph linking and iterative reformulation amplify upstream ASR errors, resulting in a 36-67% larger clean-to-noisy F1 performance gap than naive dense retrieval across three benchmarks.
key_points: Evaluated four RAG configurations using four neural TTS-synthesized English accents across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue benchmarks.
Combining entity-graph linking and iterative reformulation widened the F1 performance gap from clean text to high-WER accents by 36-67% compared to naive dense retrieval.
Entity corruption caused by ASR is the dominant failure mode, accounting for 87-96% of degradation cases on 2WikiMultiHopQA across all tested methods.
Lightweight surface-form mitigations failed to close the performance gap, showing that downstream retrieval structures inherent to multi-hop RAG amplify residual entity errors.
summary.why_it_matters: Building voice-driven multi-hop RAG systems requires addressing structural error amplification, as standard graph and iterative retrieval techniques degrade significantly when exposed to noisy ASR inputs.

papers.title: Industrial-Instruction: An End-to-End Framework for Building Instruction-Tuning and Benchmark Datasets from Industrial Technical Reports

summary.tldr: Industrial-Instruction introduces an end-to-end pipeline and two open QA datasets derived from Panasonic technical reports to benchmark and fine-tune LLMs on industrial troubleshooting, maintenance, and specification data.
key_points: Processes 906 Panasonic technical reports (7,525 pages) using layout-aware extraction, semantic retrieval indexing, and synthetic multiple-choice QA generation across five query-document relationships.
Yields two ~13.6k QA pair datasets generated by Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct and Claude-Opus-4.6, filtered down from an initial 23.9k generated samples.
Fine-tuning sub-10B parameter LLMs improves Set-Match Accuracy from 28.5% to 42.0% and F1 from 46.6% to 63.5% on the Panasonic benchmark.
Claude-Opus-4.6 data provides cleaner generation and preserves general domain MMLU performance, whereas Qwen3-30B data results in a minor catastrophic forgetting effect.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a reproducible framework to transform complex, multi-modal industrial technical documentation into effective instruction-tuning data and benchmarks for targeted enterprise LLM deployment.

papers.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses

summary.tldr: Recuris introduces a recursive Experiential-Working Memory architecture that decouples long-horizon state tracking from skill execution, using a fixed Meta-Agent to perform localized, validation-gated memory updates.
key_points: Working Memory tracks task state to guide skill selection from Experiential Memory, preventing long histories from obscuring current task needs.
Execution traces serve as structured evidence to localize failures directly to specific memory components.
A Meta-Agent executes bounded, validation-gated updates to Skill Memory based on localized failure evidence.
Recuris improved task success in 35 of 37 model-benchmark pairs across four long-horizon benchmarks, reducing common long-horizon failures by up to 80%.
Key benchmark gains include +15.6 points on Claude Opus 5 (reaching 87.9% on tau-bench) and up to a +32.2 point advantage on the longest interaction horizons.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes localized, memory-level updates as a scalable mechanism for recursive self-improvement in LLM agents without needing full context history or model re-training.

papers.title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL

summary.tldr: SPO++ enhances asynchronous agentic RL by standardizing terminal-outcome advantages under the action-token measure and organizing prompt evidence by policy event generation order rather than learner receipt order.
key_points: Identifies that trajectory centering in SPO fails to center the token-weighted quantity consumed by the token-mean actor loss.
Fixes the advantage-loss mismatch by standardizing terminal-outcome advantages directly under the action-token measure.
Reorders prompt evidence by original policy event generation time instead of learner receipt order.
Demonstrates improved online learning efficiency over SPO on ALFWorld across two model scales and on Math-TIR.
Identifies action-token-measure normalization as the primary contributor to performance gains in ablation studies.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates training delays in variable-length, tool-use RL trajectories without sacrificing policy optimization stability or sample efficiency.

papers.title: CAFE: Self-Improving Search Agents Need Co-Evolving Feedback

summary.tldr: CAFE is a framework where a shared-parameter model alternates between search-agent and critic roles to co-evolve corrective feedback alongside policy updates.
key_points: CAFE uses a shared-parameter model that alternates roles between a search agent and a critic.
Online RL optimization incorporates a prompt-level call-skip success gap to shape request returns and applies feedback-aware advantage shaping around feedback events.
Offline preference optimization trains the critic on matched successful and unsuccessful rollouts derived from base agent failures.
One-sided updates to either the agent or critic plateau, whereas joint co-evolution yields continuous performance gains.
Evaluations across seven search benchmarks show CAFE outperforms RL-based search agents, generalizes to six out-of-domain benchmarks, and reduces answer-level hallucinations.
summary.why_it_matters: Co-evolving in-trajectory feedback prevents optimization plateaus in self-improving search agents and leads to lower hallucination rates during complex retrievals.

papers.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth

summary.tldr: Meta$^n$ achieves recursive self-improvement beyond two meta-levels by holding a meta-operation fixed and repeatedly applying it to its own traces and code to generate subsequent layers.
key_points: The meta-operation Ω reads lower-layer solver stack traces and code, then generates the next layer as a strategic pre-process and helper library.
System depth is determined dynamically by convergence rather than being fixed in advance, supplemented by an evolutionary archive search over layer chains.
Meta$^n$ outperforms existing self-improving agents across eight benchmark families on two model backbones.
It achieves the only non-zero score on ARC-AGI-2, with ablations showing gains stem from inter-layer conditioning and emergent layer roles.
summary.why_it_matters: It bypasses the traditional stability-driven caps on meta-depth in LLM agents, enabling continuous strategic self-improvement without destabilizing editing machinery.

papers.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward

summary.tldr: OPDVR combines on-policy distillation and verifiable reward RL by reformulating sampled-token OPD implicit rewards with trajectory correctness and a ReLU gating mechanism, eliminating extra hyperparameters while outperforming standard OPD across six reasoning benchmarks.
key_points: Reformulates the implicit reward of sampled-token on-policy distillation (OPD) using trajectory correctness.
Applies a ReLU gating mechanism to guarantee non-negative rewards for correct trajectories and non-positive rewards for incorrect ones.
Transforms sampled-token OPD into a proper RLVR formulation that integrates seamlessly with policy gradient algorithms like GRPO without extra hyperparameters or heuristic switching.
summary.why_it_matters: It aligns dense token-level teacher guidance with task-level correctness without adding hyperparameter tuning overhead or performance trade-offs.

papers.title: The Invisible Editorial Layer: Formalizing Undisclosed Inference-Time Steering, Probability Placement, and the Attribution Problem in Deployed Language Models

summary.tldr: This paper formalizes undisclosed inference-time steering—systematic logit-level modifications applied before token sampling—and introduces frameworks for attributing behavioral bias, modeling probability placement advertising, and establishing inference policy transparency.
key_points: Formalizes the operational distinction 'Model != Deployed System' to show that deployment-layer interventions decouple observed text from model weights.
Defines the Inference Attribution Problem, demonstrating that behavioral bias cannot be causally attributed to weights alone under limited observability.
Introduces Probability Placement as an advertising primitive where commercial framing is executed via generation probability shifts rather than explicit text insertions.
Proposes Inference Policy Transparency to audit decoding-level and logit-level interventions against regulatory frameworks like the EU AI Act, EU DSA, and FTC doctrines.
summary.why_it_matters: It highlights how undisclosed post-inference logit modifications can secretly manipulate political or commercial framing in LLM outputs, complicating regulatory oversight and bias attribution.

papers.title: Parason: Revealing Subtask and Trial Parallelism in LLM Reasoning

summary.tldr: Parason introduces a framework to learn and execute both subtask and trial parallelism in LLM reasoning traces, accelerating inference on complex math benchmarks using Parallelism-Aware GRPO.
key_points: Identifies two distinct parallel reasoning modes: Subtask Parallelism (task decomposition) and Trial Parallelism (simultaneous speculative attempts, verification, and hypothesis aggregation).
Reveals that Trial Parallelism accounts for 65.5% of parallelizable reasoning steps in DeepSeek-V4 on the HLE benchmark, becoming more dominant on difficult problems.
Converts sequential reasoning traces into structured parallel trajectories using a context-free grammar.
Trains models with Parallelism-Aware Group Relative Policy Optimization (PA-GRPO) using a reward function that balances accuracy, latency, and parallelism ratios.
Executes parallel structures at inference time via tool calls, achieving an average ~1.7x wall-clock speedup on AIME24 and AIME25 while preserving accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: By unlocking trial parallelism alongside subtask parallelism, Parason significantly reduces inference latency for long test-time LLM reasoning traces without sacrificing problem-solving accuracy.

papers.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining

summary.tldr: Language model pretraining loss dynamics collapse onto a single trajectory when runs match their effective learning rate (ELR), defined as the ratio of learning rate to parameter norm.
key_points: Matching ELR produces identical loss trajectories across different learning rates and parameter norms, with mean collapse errors (a few x 10^-3) falling below seed-to-seed variance.
ELR collapse precision is primarily governed by normalization design and the timescale of LR-norm variation.
Weight decay and Hyperball influence loss dynamics predominantly through the ELR schedules they induce.
Replacing standard learning rate with ELR allows a fitted functional scaling law (FSL) to transfer across norm-control methods and explains the delayed acceleration effect.
summary.why_it_matters: ELR serves as a unified coordinate that links learning rate scheduling, norm-control interventions, and scaling laws to simplify pretraining optimization.

papers.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report

summary.tldr: Tencent has released WeMM-Embedding, a family of 2B, 4B, and 9B universal multimodal embedding models supporting text, images, videos, visual documents, and interleaved inputs with flexible output dimensions.
key_points: Model family consists of 2B, 4B, and 9B parameter variants trained via a large-scale alignment stage followed by a refined fine-grained supervision and cross-scale knowledge transfer stage.
The 9B variant achieves a state-of-the-art score of 80.6 on MMEB-v2, while the 2B model outperforms previous 8B open-source baselines.
Deployed at scale within WeChat applications, showing gains across a 26-task in-house benchmark and positive results across 14 online A/B tests.
Model weights and code have been open-sourced on GitHub.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers open-source, production-proven multimodal embedding models that outperform larger existing baselines in retrieval, search, and recommendation tasks.

papers.title: Curved Inference II: Sleeper Agent Geometry - Extending Interpretability Beyond Probes

summary.tldr: Curved Inference II introduces semantic surface area (A'), an unsupervised geometric metric in unnormalised residual space that detects naturalistic deceptive reasoning without reliance on backdoors, artificial triggers, or linear probes.
key_points: Addresses limitations of linear probes, which rely on artificial backdoor insertion rather than naturally occurring deceptive alignment.
Introduces semantic surface area (A') to quantify representational work by measuring both magnitude and directional change of meaning construction in residual space.
Uses multi-turn context windows to simulate realistic deceptive reasoning, evaluating outputs via LLM consensus across five prompt strategies and two model families.
Demonstrates that geometric measurement precision uncovers hidden semantic signatures, shifting statistical significance for certain strategies from p = 0.555 to p = 0.048.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a scalable, unsupervised detection method for deceptive alignment based on the intrinsic geometric shape of inference, even when models suppress linear indicators.

security.title: Prompt Structure Redistributes, Not Reduces: An Empirical Analysis of Security-Weaknesses in LLM-Generated Python Code

summary.tldr: An empirical study reveals that structured and security-focused prompts do not reliably reduce overall code weaknesses in LLMs, but instead redistribute risk from high-severity to low-severity flaws.
key_points: Evaluating 424 security-sensitive Python tasks across GPT-4o and LLaMA 3.1-8B using Bandit and CodeQL showed that structured prompts drastically cut output refusals (GPT-4o invalid outputs dropped from 338/424 to 37-52).

Security-oriented refinements redistributed GPT-4o risks rather than eliminating them, shifting high-severity findings down from 20.8% to 13.6% while low-severity findings increased from 32% to 43.5%.
LLaMA 3.1-8B exhibited weaker, less consistent security shifts across prompt variants compared to GPT-4o.
Stricter prompt variants induced security-driven semantic drift, causing models to silently alter or omit explicitly requested unsafe constructs.
summary.why_it_matters: Prompt engineering cannot replace traditional code auditing and security controls, as security-focused prompts merely alter the distribution of vulnerabilities rather than preventing them.

security.title: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety-Utility Balancing

summary.tldr: StepGuard is a step-level guard model trained via the StepGen data engine and Balance-GRPO to audit tool actions before execution, maintaining high agent utility while mitigating security risks.
key_points: Audits completed trajectories and pre-execution tool actions to catch security risks like unauthorized actions and information leakage before execution.
Uses StepGen, an automated data engine that creates paired safe and unsafe trajectories sharing identical contexts up to the risky step.
Employs Balance-GRPO, a reinforcement learning approach that dynamically balances learning between safe and unsafe actions using real-time accuracy metrics to minimize over-defense and under-defense.
Reduces the mean attack success rate on AgentDojo and AgentDyn by 77.3% relative to an unguarded baseline, with a utility loss of only 2.8 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables proactive, real-time security interventions for tool-using LLM agents without significantly degrading their functional task completion capabilities.

security.title: Do System Prompts Leave Behavioral Fingerprints? A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Clone Detection via Output Similarity

summary.tldr: Black-Box Behavioral Fingerprinting (BBF) uses model outputs via API access to detect prompt clones, achieving an overall cross-model AUC of 0.725 and up to 0.889 AUC against non-adaptive prompt paraphrasing.
key_points: BBF registers behavioral signatures from black-box LLM API outputs to compare suspect deployments against baseline outputs.
System prompt selection accounts for 24.4% of output variance, enabling same-model clone detection to achieve 0.876 AUC.
Cross-model detection performance varies by detector identity, yielding an average cross-model AUC of 0.725 (ranging from 0.845 for Claude to 0.665 for Qwen).
Simple style modifications, such as adding a single-sentence formal-tone prefix, degrade detection performance on short structured outputs (e.g., MNLI AUC dropped from 0.978 to 0.547).
Diagnostic Query Optimization improves cross-model detection performance by +0.120 AUC at zero cost.
summary.why_it_matters: BBF enables prompt creators to detect stolen or cloned system prompts via black-box API queries, though its effectiveness remains vulnerable to simple stylistic modifications.

security.title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Region-Aware Consistency Repair of Backdoors in MLLMs

summary.tldr: RACER is a model-level backdoor repair framework for MLLMs that uses region-aware layer-wise inconsistency normalization and adversarial fine-tuning on 100 clean samples without prior trigger knowledge.
key_points: Identifies that backdoors cause a modality-dependent 'layer-wise inconsistency anomaly' concentrated in token regions encoding trigger features.
Decomposes representations into visual and textual token regions, normalizes layer-wise inconsistency separately, and recomposes them via modality-aware weights over a deep-layer window.
Uses a min-max optimization loop to synthesize worst-case perturbations and fine-tune the model to suppress backdoor-inducing representational shifts.
Requires only 100 clean samples and no prior knowledge of the trigger, attack objective, or model infection status.
Evaluated on three open-source MLLMs across 36 backdoor settings, reducing average Attack Success Rate (ASR) to 1.1% and achieving 0% ASR in 32 settings.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables model owners to permanently remove latent multimodal backdoors directly from model weights prior to deployment using minimal clean data, rather than relying on inference-time input filtering.

security.title: What Guides the Agent? Adjudicating Unauthorized Behavior via Localizing Behavior-Guiding Instructions

summary.tldr: Attnlocate is a runtime framework that localizes behavior-guiding instructions by modeling LLM attention matrices as 1D object detection tasks to adjudicate indirect prompt injection and tool poisoning attacks.
key_points: Converts token-level activation traces in attention matrices into a feature space using a multi-head, multi-layer aggregation scheme.
Utilizes a 1-D U-Net with an anchor-free detection head to detect specific context spans driving tool-calling decisions.
Adjudicates malicious execution attempts by comparing the authority level of the detected instruction's source provider against policy rules.
Demonstrates performance across 10 agent configurations and 5 LLM families, achieving a 0.743 mean IoU, 0.956 average AUROC, and 0.934 TPR at a 0.067 FPR.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides dynamic, runtime defense against prompt injection and tool poisoning by directly pinpointing causal instructions inside internal attention activations without needing model retraining.

security.title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents

summary.tldr: WebMCP-Phalanx is a dual-layer browser runtime that enforces tool provenance with cryptographic credentials and uses isolated LLM agents to secure WebMCP browser-integrated LLM tools against prompt injection and lifecycle attacks.
key_points: Identifies three security risks in the W3C WebMCP proposal: subject-attribution spoofing, uncontrolled tool lifecycles, and semantic prompt injection.

Implements a browser-native trust anchor that binds tools to registering principals via cryptographically protected capability credentials and provenance tracking, dropping revocation and overwrite attack success from 100% to 0%.

Uses a dual-agent architecture separating an unprivileged Quarantine Agent (Q-LLM) for content inspection from an execution-privileged Agent (P-LLM), blocking 100% (80/80) of tool-description prompt injections and 97.5% (78/80) of tool-return attacks.

Identifies a white-box adaptive bypass vulnerability using malicious tool names invoked before inspection, prompting the design of a call-timing gate to delay tool invocation until all metadata is validated.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a practical security framework for safely granting browser-integrated LLM agents access to web page tools without exposing users to origin spoofing or untrusted prompt injections.

security.title: RAGSentinel: Certifiable Geometric Consensus for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: RAGSentinel is a training-free, label-free defense for black-box RAG that filters poisoned documents by detecting query-conditioned hidden-state shifts and geometric outliers using a surrogate encoder.
key_points: Measures query-conditioned hidden-state shifts induced by retrieved documents via a surrogate encoder and strips shared topic directions.
Filters poisoned documents by treating them as geometric outliers relative to a robust majority consensus.
Provides theoretical guarantees for exact recovery of a poison-free context under honest-majority and representation-level separation conditions.
Maintains defense efficacy against adaptive attackers with full pipeline knowledge across three QA datasets and three LLM families.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a mathematically provable defense that secures black-box RAG pipelines against context-injection attacks without requiring model retraining or label annotations.

security.title: NeuronGuard: Robust LLM Safety Alignment via Ablation-Aware Safety Signal Redistribution

summary.tldr: NeuronGuard is a fine-tuning defense that redistributes safety signals across neurons using dynamic linear classifiers, forced refusal under ablation, and randomized gradient projection to prevent prompt and neuron-level attacks.
key_points: Identifies safety-critical neurons dynamically during fine-tuning using periodically refreshed per-layer linear classifiers.
Forces model refusal under deliberate neuron ablation while applying KL-divergence regularization to ensure distributional consistency.
Uses a randomized gradient projection strategy to resolve gradient conflicts between task utility and safety objectives.
Provides a formal theoretical upper-bound reduction on Attack Success Rate (ASR) and demonstrates near-zero ASR across six SOTA attack strategies.
summary.why_it_matters: It mitigates LLM safety brittleness by decentralizing safety-critical representation, protecting models against both prompt jailbreaks and post-deployment white-box neuron pruning without degrading task performance.

security.title: The State of AI-Enabled Malware August 2026: From Brand Abuse to Agentic Execution

summary.tldr: Unit 42 research analyzes the evolution of AI-enabled malware from brand abuse to agentic execution, demonstrating that existing behavioral detection and endpoint analytics remain effective at stopping AI-authored code before execution.
key_points: Threat actors are evolving AI usage in malware from brand abuse to agentic execution models.
Existing behavioral detection and endpoint analytics successfully block AI-authored malicious code prior to execution.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations can rely on current behavioral and endpoint security controls to mitigate emerging AI-authored malware threats before execution.

security.title: Semantic Overlays: Mitigating Prompt Injection with Annotations Beyond Tokens and Steering Vectors

summary.tldr: Semantic Overlays introduce learned adapters applied to frozen model residual streams at prefill positions to create an out-of-band annotation channel that mitigates prompt injection.
key_points: Semantic Overlays apply small, trained adapters to selected prefill positions in a frozen model's residual stream, acting as a non-textual channel for span identity.
Using an overlay to mark untrusted context spans as non-executable defends against prompt injections while preserving underlying text readability, achieving a 92.5% exact copy rate.

On prompt injection benchmarks, the defense improves SEP separation from 24.3% to 96.5% with unchanged utility, reduces TensorTrust attack success from 34.8% to 6.6%, and drops compliance to 0% across all four PIArena attack families.
Overlays are composable and can encode complex semantics, such as language transformation imperatives or structural constraints, beyond traditional static steering vectors.
summary.why_it_matters: They provide a robust structural defense against prompt injection by separating user data from system instructions without relying on vulnerable token-level distinctions.

security.title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)

summary.tldr: A systematic security analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2 v0.2) reveals that valid mandate signatures cannot guarantee user intent when pre-authorization contexts like A2A messages and MCP tool calls are manipulated.
key_points: Used the MAESTRO framework to model AP2 v0.2 across 5 transaction phases, 5 deployment architectures, 4 threat actors, 11 attack surfaces, 18 adversary capabilities, and 6 attacker goals.
Cataloged 48 threats across five attack families and scored them via AIVSS, highlighting 8 high-risk threats that reach the High severity band in at least one architecture.
Constructed a complete testbed spanning all five architectures and created proof-of-concept demonstrations covering all 8 high-risk threats and mitigations.
Developed a deployment-aware security scanner that maps threats using static, cross-role consistency, and adversarial checks.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that post-signing mandate protections fail against pre-authorization prompt injections and context manipulations necessitates stronger defense mechanisms for autonomous LLM payment workflows.

security.title: TrustShiftProbe: Characterizing, Benchmarking, and Defending Staged Trust Attacks on MCP Servers

summary.tldr: TrustShiftProbe characterizes temporal TrustShift attacks on MCP servers—where compromised endpoints act benignly before deploying malicious payloads—and introduces SHIELD, a zero-oracle runtime defense that audits server responses against learned baselines.
key_points: TrustShift attacks exploit the MCP tool channel through a two-phase lifecycle: a benign conditioning phase that builds reliance followed by adversarial defection at a trust horizon.

The framework establishes a taxonomy of nine TrustShift variants across three execution mechanisms (structural violation, semantic corruption, scope expansion) and three objectives (disruption, exfiltration, combined).
Pre-deployment static analysis and runtime middleware filters fail against these attacks because schema-valid payload manipulations preserve outer protocol compliance.
Evaluated on frontier proprietary and open-weight models, TrustShift attacks achieved a 69.5% mean attack success rate, which the SHIELD runtime defense reduced to 42.7%.
summary.why_it_matters: This research reveals that trusted MCP server endpoints can bypass static pre-deployment checks and schema-based runtime filters by delaying malicious behavior, necessitating stateful, baseline-auditing defenses at the transport boundary.

security.title: CyberFactory: Scaling Cyber Security Capabilities with Instances from the Wild

summary.tldr: CyberFactory is an open-source framework that converts real-world CVE artifacts into executable cybersecurity tasks, using skill-guided agentic rollout trajectories to train Aegis, a specialized defense-oriented model.
key_points: Unifies data construction, trajectory synthesis, and model training across proof-of-concept (PoC) generation, vulnerability patching, and CyberQA.
Uses a reusable vulnerability-analysis skill to direct teacher models through source code inspection, prior-guided problem solving, and evidence-based validation.
Generates agentic supervision through tool and environment interactions that iterate based on execution feedback.
Yields Aegis, a model that internalizes skill-guided procedures for inference without needing explicit skills at runtime, scoring 52.4% Pass@1 on CyberGym (+22.8 points over its Qwen 3.5 base).
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a reproducible, open-source method to scale agentic cybersecurity training data and train models that outperform general-purpose LLMs on complex vulnerability exploitation and patching tasks.

security.title: When Can Agents Safely Checkpoint, Fork, Restore, and Merge? Exact Checking for Execution Edits

summary.tldr: An exact algorithm and Lean-mechanized checker that evaluate agent execution edits—Checkpoint, Fork, Restore, and Merge—to determine all safe continuation paths or prove that no safe option exists.
key_points: Execution edits (Fork, Restore, Merge) alter agent control flow but cannot undo prior authorizations or sent tool requests, risking duplicate actions or discarded results.
The proposed algorithm lists all policy-compliant task completions and filters out paths that render required future results impossible, returning a checkable proof if no safe implementation exists.
The framework formally covers Checkpoint alongside six distinct forms of Fork, Restore, and Merge, including extensions and atomic enforcement mechanics.
All finite checkers, runtime invariants, and execution edit forms are mechanized in Lean and validated via executable tests in a public repository.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables agent runtimes to safely manipulate execution state at runtime without risking policy violations, duplicate tool calls, or lost execution results.

security.title: SeriCrypt: An LLM-Driven Context-Aware Serialization Framework for Cryptographic Protocols

summary.tldr: SeriCrypt is an LLM-driven framework that extracts cryptographic protocol constraints into a custom domain-specific language (CDSL) to automate context-aware byte-stream message serialization for testing.
key_points: Uses an LLM to parse unstructured protocol specifications into CDSL, capturing field constraints, state dependencies, and cryptographic computation rules.
Features a protocol-agnostic execution engine that parses CDSL to automate field value resolution, cryptographic primitive invocation, and byte-stream serialization.
Evaluated on TLS 1.2/1.3, IKEv1/v2, SSH, and TLCP, successfully generating valid message sequences and completing full handshakes across all tested implementations.
Identified five specification violations during security constraint testing and achieved deeper state exploration and higher code coverage than mainstream fuzzers within identical time budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: It automates the generation of complex, state-dependent cryptographic messages, significantly improving the efficacy of state machine learning, conformance testing, and fuzzing for secure protocols.

infra.title: Restore LLM Inference Capacity in Seconds with Shadow Engine Recovery in NVIDIA Dynamo

key_points: Standard LLM engine failure recovery relies on a cold restart, requiring minutes to load weights into HBM, compile kernels, and capture CUDA graphs.
Unplanned process failures force surviving workers to temporarily absorb displaced inference traffic during prolonged cold restarts.
Shadow engine recovery provides a fast-failover mechanism in NVIDIA Dynamo to bypass lengthly initialization phases.
summary.why_it_matters: By drastically reducing failure recovery time from minutes to seconds, shadow engine recovery prevents traffic overloads on surviving workers during LLM inference node outages.
